notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: Overview The Engineering Technology, B.S. program prepares individuals to apply basic mathematics, science, engineering, and technology principles and technical skills that enable them to engage in a variety of engineering technology projects. Coursework includes various engineering technology topics, including laboratory and design projects that lead to careers in manufacturing systems and sustainable energy and transportation engineering technology areas. The 40-41 units of core courses are discipline-specific content of the curriculum that focuses on the applied aspects of science and engineering. During the junior and senior years, students may choose from a broad spectrum of electives to match individual talents and interests with a career objective. Finally, the program has a capstone experience that develops student competencies in applying both technical and non-technical skills to solve real-world problems and prepare them for future careers. Requirements for the Degree The degree requires 120 units, of which, 87-88 units are in the major with 15 units satisfying the General Education (GE) requirements. The GE requirements are met by taking the following courses or their cross-listing courses: IHE - ENGR 1500 Area 2 - MATH 2110 Area 4 - CE 3000 / EE 3000 / ME 3000 Areas 5A and 5C - PHYS 1100 / ( PHYS 1560 and PHYS 1570 ) UD Area 2 - ECON 3060 *Note: Complete one or two courses from the following for 4 or 5 units.
notes.contentHtml:
Overview


The Engineering Technology, B.S. program prepares individuals to apply basic mathematics, science, engineering, and technology principles and technical skills that enable them to engage in a variety of engineering technology projects.


Coursework includes various engineering technology topics, including laboratory and design projects that lead to careers in manufacturing systems and sustainable energy and transportation engineering technology areas. The 40-41 units of core courses are discipline-specific content of the curriculum that focuses on the applied aspects of science and engineering. 


During the junior and senior years, students may choose from a broad spectrum of electives to match individual talents and interests with a career objective. Finally, the program has a capstone experience that develops student competencies in applying both technical and non-technical skills to solve real-world problems and prepare them for future careers.


Requirements for the Degree


The degree requires 120 units, of which, 87-88 units are in the major with 15 units satisfying the General Education (GE) requirements. The GE requirements are met by taking the following courses or their cross-listing courses:


  • IHE - ENGR 1500  
  • Area 2 - MATH 2110  
  • Area 4 - CE 3000  / EE 3000  / ME 3000 
  • Areas 5A and 5C - PHYS 1100   / (PHYS 1560  and PHYS 1570) 
  • UD Area 2 - ECON 3060  



*Note: Complete one or two courses from the following for 4 or 5 units.
